description:
Plan view: A straight horizontal curb line (labeled CURB LINE) runs across the sheet. Above it, parking tee marks are drawn 2.1 m (7') out from the curb line. One parking layout is dimensioned as 12 m (40') overall, split into two 6 m (20') spaces, with a tee mark at each end of the 12 m run and one at the 6 m split point. The marks read, left to right, as end tee, end tee, middle tee, end tee for the first run, and the pattern continues to the right with the next run (end tee, middle tee, end tee, end tee). A dashed rounded outline around one end tee and one middle tee carries the callout SEE DETAIL "A". Short heavy bars on the curb line, labeled RED CURB (TYP), mark the red curb at the ends of each run, each 2.4 m (8') long (dimensioned at the right end of the 12 m run).

Detail A: An enlarged plan of an end tee and the next middle tee, 6 m (20') apart stem to stem. Both tees are made of 100 mm (4") white stripe (TYP.). Each stem is 1 m (3') long. End tee: a single bar 0.6 m (2') long extends to one side of the stem, set 0.6 m (2') from one end of the stem and 0.4 m (1') from the other end. Middle tee: the bar is 1.2 m (4') long overall, 0.6 m (2') to each side of the stem, with the same 0.6 m (2') and 0.4 m (1') offsets along the stem. The clear space between the end of the first tee's bar and the start of the second tee's bar is 4.9 m (16').

title: Parking Tee Installation
summary: Layout of parking tee markings that delineate parallel parking spaces along a curb. description:
Condition A, plan view (centerline only, marked or unmarked): A two-way street is shown between two edge lines with a dashed centerline (CL). Two heavy horizontal lines across the full width, labeled YELLOW SCHOOL CROSSWALKS, mark the crosswalk. Working back from the crosswalk, the pavement words XING, SCHOOL and SLOW are stacked in the lane along one line labeled CENTERLINE OF MESSAGE (*). The distance from the crosswalk to XING is marked VARIES. XING to SCHOOL is 8 m (25') MIN and SCHOOL to SLOW is 8 m (25') MIN. The message centerline is offset 1.7 m (5.5') from the street centerline.

Condition B, plan view (multi-lane): The same crosswalk (YELLOW SCHOOL CROSSWALKS) crosses a multi-lane street with a double centerline (CL) and lane lines that are solid near the crosswalk and dashed farther back. The words XING, SCHOOL and SLOW are repeated in each of the two lanes on one side of the double centerline. The distance from the crosswalk to XING is VARIES, and the spacing is 8 m (25') MIN between XING and SCHOOL and 8 m (25') MIN between SCHOOL and SLOW. In the lane next to the centerline the callout reads CENTER WORD MESSAGE IN LANE. In the outer lane the message centerline (*) is dimensioned 1.7 m (5.5') off the lane line.

description:
Installation details box: A boxed list titled INSTALLATION DETAILS with seven numbered requirements for speed humps (see notes).

Figure A, speed hump warning sign (typical): A drawing of a diamond-shaped warning sign reading SPEED HUMP with a pair of warning flags mounted on its upper corners. Below it on the same post is a small rectangular plaque reading 15 MPH, labeled W13-1(15) SIGN. Callouts: WARNING FLAGS (FIRST 30-DAYS), 30in X 30in, BLACK ON YELLOW OR W17-1 "SPEED HUMP", 6 in SERIES E LETTERS, and SIGN LOCATIONS: AS DIRECTED BY ENGINEER.

Temporary signage details box: A boxed list titled TEMPORARY SIGNAGE DETAILS with two numbered requirements for flashing barricades and signs during construction.

Title block: City of Pasadena Department of Transportation, Speed Hump/Cushion Installation Channelization/Temporary Signing Requirements, Standard Plan S-707, Sheet 1 of 5, Revision 10 (April 2023), units IMPERIAL, approved by the Deputy Director of Transportation on 04/19/2023.
notes:
Installation details:
1. Speed humps shall not be placed over manholes, watergates, junction chambers, etc.
2. Edge of speed hump should be 10 ft minimum from edge and uphill of driveway.
3. Height of speed hump shall nominally be 3.5 in +/- 0.25 in at all cross sections.
4. Whenever possible, speed humps shall be placed at property lines instead of mid-lot.
5. Whenever possible, speed humps shall be placed adjacent to street lights.
6. Speed humps shall be marked using thermoplastic material.
7. Speed hump signs shall be installed per Figure A, where noted on plans.
Figure A: Speed hump warning sign (typical). Warning flags (first 30 days). 30 in x 30 in. Black on yellow or W17-1 SPEED HUMP, 6 in Series E letters. W13-1(15) sign. Sign locations: as directed by Engineer.
Temporary signage details:
1. The contractor shall furnish and maintain a flashing barricade, 50 feet from each speed hump location in both directions, until the first application of paint has been applied showing the pavement messages and striping.
2. Mount 30 in x 30 in W8-1 or W17-1 warning sign (black on yellow, 6 in Series E letters) and W13-1 sign per MUTCD with the California Supplement, on each of the barricades at each speed hump location.
title: Speed Hump/Cushion Installation Channelization/Temporary Signing Requirements (Sheet 1 of 5)
summary: First sheet of the Pasadena speed hump and speed cushion standard. It lists seven installation requirements, such as no placement over manholes, 10 ft from driveways and a 3.5 in nominal height, and shows the W17-1 SPEED HUMP warning sign with flags and a W13-1(15) 15 MPH plaque. Temporary signing requires a flashing barricade 50 ft from each hump in both directions, with W8-1 or W17-1 and W13-1 signs, until the pavement markings are applied.

description:
Plan view: A roadway segment drawn between the existing gutter and curb face lines at the top and bottom, with edge of pavement lines, and a dashed centerline of roadway (CL of ROADWAY) across the middle. The speed hump is 12 ft long along the direction of travel, bounded by two solid vertical lines with a dashed vertical line at CENTER OF SPEED HUMP. On each side of the centerline there is a row of two nested chevron markings, each 6 ft long along the travel direction. The row above the centerline points left and the row below points right. Each chevron is a 12in WHITE MARKINGS band with a 1ft gap to the inner solid triangle. Each marking is 6ft WIDE MARKING and is set 3ft FROM CENTER OF ROADWAY**. Section cut A-A runs across the pavement edge at the curb and section cut B-B is taken along the marking at the centerline.

Section A-A: Transverse section at the curb end. From the curb face, a 2ft MAX (WIDTH VARIES) gutter portion, then a 2ft TAPER up to the A.C. STANDARD overlay, 3/8in MIX D2 PG 64-10 with 5.6% ASPHALT BINDER, over a TACK COAT.

Section B-B: Longitudinal profile of the hump, 12 FT long with the crest 6 FT from the start. Height arrows at even 6.0in TYP spacing read 0.0in, 0.6in, 1.1in, 1.5in, 1.9in, 2.3in, 2.6in, 2.9in, 3.1in, 3.3in, 3.4in, 3.5in and 3.5in. The profile rises from 0.0in to the 3.5in crest at 6 FT and falls back to 0.0in at 12 FT.

description:
Plan view: A roadway half-width from the existing gutter and curb face at the bottom to beyond the centerline, with the vertical line CENTER OF SPEED CUSHIONS. Each cushion is 12 ft long in the direction of travel and has curved ends. Three cushions are stacked across the roadway. The top cushion has a length across the road marked VARIES, a 6ft WIDE MARKING chevron, and a 3ft dimension from the chevron tip to the lower edge of the cushion. A 2ft gap follows. The center cushion is 7ft wide and straddles the CL of ROADWAY, with a 3ft WIDE MARKING and a 1ft 6in dimension at its taper. Another 2ft gap follows. The bottom cushion next to the edge of pavement has its length marked VARIES and a nested chevron of 12in WHITE MARKINGS with a 1ft gap. Cut lines A-A (through the center cushion), B-B (along the center of the cushions across the roadway) and C-C (along the bottom cushion) are indicated.

Section A-A, center cushion cross-section: Total width 7ft, made of a 1ft 6in TAPER, a 4ft flat top and a 1ft 6in TAPER. The height is 3.5in, over a TACK COAT, in A.C. STANDARD 3/8in MIX D2 PG 64-10 with 5.6% ASPHALT BINDER.

Section B-B, roadway half cross-section: Measured from the curb face to the CL of roadway over a total of 14ft-19ft. Left to right: 2ft MAX (WIDTH VARIES) at the gutter, 1ft 6in TAPER, VARIES (first cushion), 1ft 6in TAPER, 2ft gap, 1ft 6in TAPER, 2ft (half of the 4 ft center cushion top) to the centerline. The pavement is A.C. STANDARD 3/8in MIX D2 PG 64-10 with 5.6% ASPHALT BINDER over a TACK COAT.

Section C-C, speed cushion cross-section: Longitudinal profile, 12 FT long with the crest 6 FT from the start. Height arrows at 6.0in TYP spacing read 0.0in, 0.6in, 1.1in, 1.5in, 1.9in, 2.3in, 2.6in, 2.9in, 3.1in, 3.3in, 3.4in, 3.5in and 3.5in.

description:
Plan view, basic crosswalk (sheet 1 of 3): A corner of an intersection is drawn with a curb return running from B.C. (beginning of curve) to E.C. (end of curve). The central angle is labeled phi, split by a bisecting radial line into two angles labeled phi/2. The curb face is shown as a heavy solid line with the edge of gutter as a dashed line outside it. The approach to the intersection runs along the top left, with the DOUBLE YELLOW CENTER LINE (DYCL) drawn as two yellow lines. The leaving side of the intersection runs down the right side, also with a DYCL. The crosswalk is formed by two heavy parallel lines, 12' apart, across each leg. The two lines turn through a 45 degree chamfer at the corner so that the crosswalk is one continuous L-shaped path around the curb return. A gray limit line (callout 2) runs from the DYCL to the curb face on the approach, 4' back from the near crosswalk line. A second 4' dimension is shown at the corner diagonal. The crosswalk lines on the approach leg and on the leaving leg are each marked with callout 1.

Title block: City of Pasadena Public Works and Transportation Department, Crosswalk Installation, Standard Plan S-709, Sheet 1 of 3, Revision 2, file S709-REV2.DWG 12/12/19, approved by the Transportation Administrator on 12/26/19.
notes:
Notes:
1. All striping shall be 12 in white or yellow, in thermoplastic or similar material.
2. White 12 in limit line in advance of crosswalks typically installed only in advance of signalized intersections, other locations and only when specified. In thermoplastic material or similar material.
Labels: Double yellow center line (DYCL). Approach to intersection. Leaving side of intersection. Curb face. Edge of gutter. B.C. E.C. Angle phi and phi/2. Dimensions: 4 ft (limit line to crosswalk line), 12 ft (between the two crosswalk lines), 4 ft (at the corner diagonal).
title: Crosswalk Installation (Basic Crosswalk), Sheet 1 of 3
summary: Pasadena standard layout for a basic marked crosswalk at a corner with a curb return. The crosswalk is two 12 in lines placed 12 ft apart that chamfer around the corner, with a limit line 4 ft back on the approach. All striping is 12 in white or yellow thermoplastic or similar, and the white limit line is typically installed only ahead of signalized intersections.

description:
Plan view, zebra crosswalk (sheet 2 of 3): The same corner geometry as sheet 1, with a curb return from B.C. to E.C., the curb face as a heavy solid line and the edge of gutter dashed. The approach to the intersection runs along the top left with a double yellow center line (DYCL) and a gray limit line from the DYCL to the curb face. The leaving side of the intersection runs down the right with another DYCL. The crosswalk outline is drawn as thin double lines that follow both legs and turn through a 45 degree chamfer at the corner. Callout 2 points to this outline (crosswalk layout per sheet 1 of 3). Inside the outline, three heavy zebra bars (callout 1) are drawn parallel to the traffic flow on each leg. On the leaving leg the bars are dimensioned 3' apart. At the leaving side, a 1.5' MIN dimension is shown from the edge of gutter to the end of the crosswalk outline.

Title block: City of Pasadena Public Works and Transportation Department, Zebra Crosswalk, Standard Plan S-709, Sheet 2 of 3, Revision 2, file S709-REV2.DWG 12/12/19, approved by the Transportation Administrator on 12/26/19.
notes:
Notes:
1. All striping shall be 12 in white or yellow, in thermoplastic or similar material. Spacing of crosswalk bars shall start from center line of street, avoiding wheel path. For intersections not perpendicular or 90 degrees (skewed or offset), all crosswalk (XWALK) bars shall be parallel to flow of traffic.
2. For crosswalk layout, refer to Sheet 1 of 3.
Labels: Double yellow center line (DYCL). Approach to intersection. Leaving side of intersection. Curb face. Edge of gutter. B.C. E.C. Dimensions: 3 ft (between zebra bars), 1.5 ft minimum (MIN) at the leaving side.
title: Zebra Crosswalk Installation, Sheet 2 of 3
summary: Pasadena standard layout for a zebra crosswalk at a corner. Heavy bars 12 in wide run parallel to traffic flow, spaced 3 ft apart, inside a crosswalk outline that follows the curb return. Bar spacing starts from the street center line and avoids the wheel path, and the leaving-side outline is kept at least 1.5 ft from the edge of gutter.

description:
Plan view, continental crosswalk (sheet 3 of 3): A corner with a curb return from B.C. to E.C., the curb face as a heavy solid line and the edge of gutter dashed. The approach to the intersection runs along the top left with a double yellow center line (DYCL), and a gray limit line (callout 3) is drawn from the DYCL to the curb face, 4' back from the first continental bar. On the approach leg, seven heavy continental bars are drawn parallel to traffic flow. The first bar is placed centered on the DYCL, the bars are callout 1, and the last bar nearest the curb is shorter so that it meets the edge of gutter (callout 2). On the leaving side, eight vertical bars are drawn across the leg, each 14' long, with a 2' space between bars and the notation UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED (MAY BE UP TO 5' AT THE DIRECTION OF THE ENGINEER). The first leaving-side bar is shortened at the curb return (callout 2). A 1.5' dimension is shown at the edge of gutter on the leaving side, and a DYCL runs down the right side.

Title block: City of Pasadena Public Works and Transportation Department, Continental Crosswalk Installation, Standard Plan S-709, Sheet 3 of 3, Revision 1, file S709-REV4.DWG 12/12/19, approved by the Transportation Administrator on 12/26/19.
notes:
Notes:
1. All continental bars shall be 2 ft wide and full length 14 ft, white or yellow, in thermoplastic or similar material.
2. Start of first bar shall be centered to DYCL, avoiding wheel path. Continental crosswalk (XWALK) bars shall meet edge of gutter. For skewed or offset intersections, all crosswalk bars shall be parallel to flow of traffic, in thermoplastic or similar materials.
3. White 12 in limit line in advance of crosswalks typically installed only in advance of signalized intersections, other locations and only when specified. In thermoplastic or similar material.
4. For crosswalk layout, refer to Sheet 1 of 3.
Labels: Unless otherwise specified (may be up to 5 ft at the direction of the Engineer). Double yellow center line (DYCL). Approach to intersection. Leaving side of intersection. Edge of gutter. B.C. E.C. Dimensions: 4 ft (limit line to first bar), 14 ft (bar length), 2 ft (space between bars), 1.5 ft (at edge of gutter).
title: Continental Crosswalk Installation, Sheet 3 of 3
summary: Pasadena standard layout for a continental crosswalk at a corner. Bars are 2 ft wide and 14 ft long, parallel to traffic flow, spaced 2 ft apart unless otherwise specified (up to 5 ft at the Engineer's direction). The first bar is centered on the double yellow center line, avoiding the wheel path, bars meet the edge of gutter, and a white 12 in limit line is typically used only ahead of signalized intersections.

description:
Detail 1, two-way no passing with painted stripe: Two parallel solid yellow lines (50 mm (2") TYP. wide) with a Type D two-way yellow marker on each outer side of the pair (one row above, one row below), spaced 7.3 m (24') and 7.3 m (24') along the line.

Detail 2, painted median: Two parallel solid yellow lines, with a single row of Type D markers on the through traffic side only, spaced 7.3 m (24') and 7.3 m (24'). Stripe width 50 mm (2") TYP.

Detail 3, 200 mm (8") white left turn lane stripe: A hatched white stripe with a row of Type G one-way clear markers on the through traffic side (above the stripe), spaced 7.3 m (24') and 7.3 m (24'). The reference width 50 mm (2") TYP. is shown at the marker.

Detail 4, 200 mm (8") white right turn lane stripe: The same hatched white stripe, with the Type G markers on the through traffic side below the stripe, spaced 7.3 m (24') and 7.3 m (24'), 50 mm (2") TYP.

Detail 5, white lane line stripe: One 14.6 m (48') cycle between two Type G markers. From the left marker: 2.6 m (8.5'), a 2.1 m (7') white stripe, 5.2 m (17') gap, a second 2.1 m (7') white stripe, then 2.6 m (8.5') to the right marker.

Detail 6, dashed centerline: Two cycles of 7.3 m (24') between Type D markers. Each cycle is 2.6 m (8.5'), a 2.1 m (7') yellow dash, then 2.6 m (8.5'), with a marker at the start of each cycle and at the end.

Detail 7, reversal into left turn lane: Two yellow lines run together on the right, and the lower line curves away to the left to form the reversal. Type D markers are spaced 7.3 m (24') on the straight part and 3.6 m (12') and 3.6 m (12') along the curved part, with stripe width 50 mm (2") TYP. A note states that the 3.6 m (12') striping is used only in the reversal.

Detail 8, left edge line with single yellow stripe: A single solid yellow line (50 mm (2") TYP.) with Type D markers above it spaced 7.3 m (24') and 7.3 m (24'), and the word Median below the line.

Title block: City of Pasadena Public Works and Transportation Department, Raised Pavement Marker Installation Detail, Standard Plan S-710, Sheet 1 of 3, Revision 2, units DUAL, file S710-1-REV2.DWG 3/21/01, approved by the Transportation Administrator on 6/4/01.
notes:
Note: Raised pavement markers to be installed at a minimum distance of 150 mm (6 in) from any crosswalk line or limit line.
Details on this sheet: Detail 1: Two-way no passing with painted stripe. Detail 2: Painted median (through traffic side). Detail 3: 200 mm (8 in) white left turn lane stripe (through traffic side). Detail 4: 200 mm (8 in) white right turn lane stripe (through traffic side). Detail 5: White lane line stripe. Detail 6: Dashed centerline. Detail 7: Reversal into left turn lane. Detail 8: Left edge line with single yellow stripe (median side).
Note on Detail 7: 3.6 m (12 ft) striping to be used only in the reversal.
Legend (shown on sheet 2 of 3): Type D 2-way yellow marker is drawn as a square with an X. Type G 1-way clear marker is drawn as a half-filled square. Yellow stripe is a solid line and white stripe is a hatched bar.
title: Raised Pavement Marker Installation Detail, Sheet 1 of 3 (Details 1 to 8)
summary: Pasadena detail for placing raised pavement markers (RPMs) with eight stripe types, including two-way no passing, painted median, left and right turn lane stripes, white lane line, dashed centerline, reversal into a left turn lane and left edge line. Markers are mostly spaced 7.3 m (24 ft), with 3.6 m (12 ft) spacing in a reversal, and are kept at least 150 mm (6 in) from any crosswalk or limit line. Type D markers are two-way yellow and Type G markers are one-way clear.

description:
Detail 9, left edge line without painted stripe: A thin line labeled Edge of Pavement with Type G one-way clear markers above it on the Through Traffic Side, spaced 7.3 m (24') and 7.3 m (24'). The word MEDIAN is below the line. The reference width is 50 mm (2") (TYP.).

Detail 10, two-way left turn lane: Two solid yellow edge lines with a 29.2 m (96') overall length shown, divided in four 7.3 m (24') marker intervals. Type D two-way yellow markers sit on and beside both lines at 7.3 m (24') spacing, with a marker on each side of each line at the left and right ends. Between the solid lines, a 3.6 m (12') yellow dash is drawn just inside each line. Along the lane the dimensions read 5.5 m (18'), 3.6 m (12'), 11.0 m (36'), 3.6 m (12') and 5.5 m (18'), so the dashes are offset 5.5 m (18') from each end and separated by 11.0 m (36').

Marker details: Two marker views, front and side, each 100 mm (4") by 100 mm (4") in plan with a reflective surface angle of 25 degrees to 32 degrees typ. Overall height is 18.4 mm (0.73") (MAX) and the base plate thickness is 3.0 mm (0.12"). Type D is a two-way yellow reflective marker with two reflective surfaces, one on each of two opposite faces. Type G is a one-way clear reflective marker with one reflective surface.

Legend: Type D 2-way yellow (square with an X), Type G 1-way clear (half-filled square), yellow stripe (solid line), white stripe (hatched bar).

Title block: City of Pasadena Public Works and Transportation Department, Raised Pavement Marker Installation Detail, Standard Plan S-710, Sheet 2 of 3, Revision 2, units DUAL, file S710-2-REV2.DWG 3/21/01, approved by the Transportation Administrator on 6/4/01.
notes:
Detail 9: Left edge line without painted stripe (median, through traffic side), markers at 7.3 m (24 ft) spacing, 50 mm (2 in) (TYP.).
Detail 10: Two-way left turn lane. Overall 29.2 m (96 ft). Dash offsets 5.5 m (18 ft), 3.6 m (12 ft), 11.0 m (36 ft), 3.6 m (12 ft) and 5.5 m (18 ft).
Type D: two-way yellow reflective marker. 100 mm (4 in) by 100 mm (4 in). Reflective surface 25 degrees to 32 degrees typ. Thickness 3.0 mm (0.12 in). Overall height 18.4 mm (0.73 in) (MAX).
Type G: one-way clear reflective marker. 100 mm (4 in) by 100 mm (4 in). Reflective surface 25 degrees to 32 degrees typ. Thickness 3.0 mm (0.12 in). Overall height 18.4 mm (0.73 in) (MAX).
Legend: Type D 2-way yellow. Type G 1-way clear. Yellow stripe. White stripe.
title: Raised Pavement Marker Installation Detail, Sheet 2 of 3 (Details 9 and 10, Marker Types)
summary: Second sheet of the Pasadena raised pavement marker detail. It shows the left edge line without a painted stripe and the two-way left turn lane, where markers repeat every 7.3 m (24 ft) over a 29.2 m (96 ft) pattern with 3.6 m (12 ft) yellow dashes. It also dimensions the Type D two-way yellow and Type G one-way clear markers, each 100 mm (4 in) square and 18.4 mm (0.73 in) high at most, and gives the marker legend.

description:
Detail 11, lead-in single yellow line: A plan of a single yellow line approaching an intersection, drawn with a curb return, a crosswalk and a cross street on the right, and arrows showing the two directions of travel. The left part shows a dashed yellow pattern with Type D markers. Each cycle is 2.6 m (8.5') TYP. from a marker to the dash, a 2.1 m (7') yellow dash, then 5.2 m (17') to the next dash, within a 7.3 m (24') cycle, and a 14.6 m (48') dimension spans two cycles. At the intersection end, a solid single yellow lead-in line, 50 mm (2") wide, runs 21.9 m (72') MIN. to 29.3 m (96') MAX. back from the intersection, with markers at even spacing (see notes) and the first and last markers at the ends.

Detail 12, lead-in/lead-out solid white lane line: A plan of an intersection with a left turn pocket, a median nose and curb returns, and arrows for both directions. On the left side the white lane line is dashed with 2.1 m (7') TYP. stripes, 5.2 m (17') gaps and 2.6 m (8.5') marker offsets, then a 5.2 m (17') gap (with a 7.3 m (24') cycle shown) leads into a solid white lead-in of 14.6 m (48') MIN. to 21.9 m (72') MAX., 50 mm (2") wide, with markers at even spacing (see notes). On the right side a 15.2 m (50') solid white lead-in is shown with markers at the start, at 7.6 m (25') and at 7.6 m (25') more, so even spacing.

Title block: City of Pasadena Public Works and Transportation Department, Raised Pavement Marker Installation Detail, Standard Plan S-710, Sheet 3 of 3, Revision 2, units DUAL, file S710-3-REV2.DWG 3/22/01, approved by the Transportation Administrator on 6/4/01.
notes:
Detail 11, lead-in single yellow line. Notes:
1. Always place beginning and end R.P.M. (raised pavement marker).
2. Distance between R.P.M. varies with length of single yellow lead-in. Minimum spacing: 6.1 m (20 ft). Standard spacing: 7.3 m (24 ft). Maximum spacing: 9.1 m (30 ft).
3. R.P.M. shall not be placed on painted stripes.
Detail 11 dimensions: 2.6 m (8.5 ft) typ., 5.2 m (17 ft), 2.1 m (7 ft), 7.3 m (24 ft), 14.6 m (48 ft), 21.9 m (72 ft) minimum to 29.3 m (96 ft) maximum, stripe 50 mm (2 in). Callout: Even spacing (see notes).
Detail 12, lead-in/lead-out solid white lane line. Notes:
1. Always place beginning and end R.P.M. (raised pavement marker).
2. Distance between R.P.M. varies with length of solid white lead-in/lead-out. Minimum spacing: 6.1 m (20 ft). Standard spacing: 7.3 m (24 ft). Maximum spacing: 9.1 m (30 ft).
3. If left turn pocket is included, the length of lead-in solid white lane line shall equal the length of the left turn pocket unless otherwise specified.
Detail 12 dimensions: 2.1 m (7 ft) typ., 5.2 m (17 ft), 2.6 m (8.5 ft), 7.3 m (24 ft), 14.6 m (48 ft) minimum to 21.9 m (72 ft) maximum, 15.2 m (50 ft), 7.6 m (25 ft) and 7.6 m (25 ft), 50 mm (2 in). Callout: Even spacing (see notes).
title: Raised Pavement Marker Installation Detail, Sheet 3 of 3 (Details 11 and 12, Lead-in Patterns)
summary: Third sheet of the Pasadena raised pavement marker detail, covering lead-in patterns at intersections. Detail 11 shows a dashed yellow line leading to a solid single yellow lead-in of 21.9 m (72 ft) to 29.3 m (96 ft). Detail 12 shows a solid white lead-in or lead-out lane line, equal to the left turn pocket length if one is included. Markers are always placed at the beginning and end, spaced 6.1 m (20 ft) to 9.1 m (30 ft) with 7.3 m (24 ft) standard, and never on painted stripes.

description:
Two-way left turn lane (yellow), plan view: Two solid yellow edge lines, each 76 mm (3") wide, run along the top and bottom of the lane. Inside each solid line is a broken yellow line made of 3.6 m (12') dashes separated by 11.0 m (36') gaps. The dashes on the upper and lower lines line up with each other, and two dashes are shown per line. Dimension labels read 3.6 m (12'), 11.0 m (36') and 3.6 m (12').

Single yellow center line, plan view: A two-way approach to an intersection with a curb return and a cross street on the right, with arrows showing both directions of travel. The yellow center line is dashed in a repeating 7.3 m (24') cycle made of a 2.1 m (7') dash and a 5.2 m (17') gap. It becomes a solid yellow lead-in line running 21.9 m (72') MIN. to 29.3 m (96') MAX. back from the intersection.

White lane line, plan view: A similar approach with a left turn pocket, showing arrows for both directions. The white lane line is dashed with 2.1 m (7') dashes, 5.2 m (17') gaps and a 7.3 m (24') cycle. A solid white lead-in of 14.6 m (48') MIN. to 21.9 m (72') MAX. runs back from the intersection on the left side. On the right side a solid white lead-in of 15.2 m (50') is dimensioned, followed by a 5.2 m (17') gap and a 2.1 m (7') dash.

Title block: City of Pasadena Public Works and Transportation Department, Two-Way Left Turn Lane, Single Yellow Centerline, Solid White Lane Line, Standard Plan S-711, Sheet 1 of 1, Revision 1, units DUAL, file S711-1-REV1.DWG 5/24/01, approved by the Transportation Administrator on 6/4/01.
notes:
1. If left turn pocket is included, the length of the lead-in solid white lane line shall equal the length of the left turn pocket unless otherwise specified.
2. If raised pavement markers are required, see Standard Plan S-710, Details 10, 11, and 12.
Labels: Two-way left turn lane (yellow), 76 mm (3 in) line width. Single yellow center line. White lane line. Dimensions: 3.6 m (12 ft), 11.0 m (36 ft), 7.3 m (24 ft), 2.1 m (7 ft), 5.2 m (17 ft), 21.9 m (72 ft) minimum to 29.3 m (96 ft) maximum, 14.6 m (48 ft) minimum to 21.9 m (72 ft) maximum, 15.2 m (50 ft).
title: Two-Way Left Turn Lane, Single Yellow Centerline, Solid White Lane Line
summary: Pasadena layout for a two-way left turn lane marked with 76 mm (3 in) yellow lines, with 3.6 m (12 ft) dashes and 11.0 m (36 ft) gaps, plus single yellow center line and white lane line patterns. Dashed lines use a 7.3 m (24 ft) cycle with 2.1 m (7 ft) dashes, leading into solid yellow lead-ins of 21.9 m (72 ft) to 29.3 m (96 ft) and solid white lead-ins of 14.6 m (48 ft) to 21.9 m (72 ft). If a left turn pocket is included, the white lead-in equals the pocket length, and raised pavement markers follow S-710 Details 10, 11 and 12.

description:
Plan view: An intersection approach is drawn with a cross street at the top, curb returns at both corners and a heavy double crosswalk or limit line across the approach. The approach has, from left to right, a double centerline that bends to the left to open a left turn pocket, a left turn lane with a solid white line on its right side and left turn arrows, a through lane with no arrows, and a right turn lane between a solid white line and the curb with right turn arrows. Each turn lane has two arrows. The arrow nearest the intersection in each lane is marked with an asterisk, and a dimension of 2.4 m (8') is shown at each side from the line at the intersection end to that first arrow. The second arrow is placed farther back in the lane.

Title block: City of Pasadena Public Works and Transportation Department, Pavement Markings for Left and Right Turn Lanes, Standard Plan S-712, Sheet 1 of 1, Revision 1, units DUAL, file S712-1-REV1.DWG 5/25/01, approved by the Transportation Administrator on 6/4/01.
notes:
Notes:
1. Arrow pavement markings to be solid white.
2. Pavement markings to be centered in lane.
* Install additional arrow if pocket is 18.3 m (60 ft) or longer.
Dimension: 2.4 m (8 ft) at each arrow.
title: Pavement Markings for Left and Right Turn Lanes
summary: Pasadena standard for turn arrow pavement markings in left and right turn lanes. Arrows are solid white and centered in the lane, with the first arrow 2.4 m (8 ft) from the line at the intersection end. An additional arrow is installed if the pocket is 18.3 m (60 ft) or longer.

description:
Condition, known property line and/or sidewalk location, plan view: The corner of a street with a curb line, a curb return, a property line and a back line of sidewalk. A heavy 300 mm (12") white stripe is the limit line, labeled STANDARD LOCATION FOR LIMIT LINE UNLESS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED. It ends at the curb line. The word STOP is shown below (behind) the limit line, with a dimension of 2.4 m (8') between the limit line and the top of STOP, and the callout INSTALL ONLY WHEN AUTHORIZED BY TRAFFIC ENGINEER points to the STOP legend. A dashed vertical line at the left is the street center line.

Condition, unknown property line or sidewalk location, plan view: The same corner with a cross-hatched rectangle marking the zone where the limit line may be placed, labeled LIMIT LINE LOCATION TO BE WITHIN THIS AREA (TYP.). The zone starts 1.2 m (4') (MIN.) back from the cross street curb line and extends to 9.1 m (30') (MAX.) back. Its width runs from the street center line (dashed line at the left) to the curb line at the right. The callout EXTEND LIMIT LINE TO STREET CENTER LINE UNLESS CHANNELIZATION REQUIRES OTHERWISE points to the center line side. The condition text reads UNKNOWN PROPERTY LINE OR SIDEWALK LOCATION. EXACT LOCATION TO BE SPECIFIED ON WORK ORDER.

Title block: City of Pasadena Public Works and Transportation Department, Limit Line and STOP Pavement Markings, Standard Plan S-713, Sheet 1 of 1, Revision 1, units DUAL, file S713-1-REV1.DWG 5/24/01, approved by the Transportation Administrator on 6/4/01.
notes:
Notes:
1. If existing limit line falls outside hatched area, notify Traffic Engineering before repainting.
Labels: Standard location for limit line, unless otherwise specified. 300 mm (12 in) white stripe. Curb line. Property line. Back line of sidewalk. Install only when authorized by Traffic Engineer. Condition: known property line and/or sidewalk location. Condition: unknown property line or sidewalk location, exact location to be specified on work order. Limit line location to be within this area (TYP.). Extend limit line to street center line unless channelization requires otherwise. Dimensions: 2.4 m (8 ft), 1.2 m (4 ft) minimum (MIN.), 9.1 m (30 ft) maximum (MAX.).
title: Limit Line and STOP Pavement Markings
summary: Pasadena standard for locating limit lines and STOP pavement markings. Where the property line or sidewalk is known, the limit line is a 300 mm (12 in) white stripe with the STOP legend 2.4 m (8 ft) behind it, installed only when authorized by the Traffic Engineer. Where it is unknown, the limit line goes anywhere in a hatched zone 1.2 m (4 ft) minimum to 9.1 m (30 ft) maximum back from the cross street curb line, set by work order, and extends to the street center line unless channelization requires otherwise.

description:
Transition diagram, plan view: A turn bay transition is drawn between a lower baseline (the existing lane edge) and an upper line (the centerline or median line shown as a double line), 3 m (10') apart at the end of the transition. Stations along the baseline are marked with vertical lines. From the START OF TRANSITION at point A, the dimensions to the right are 4.5 m (15') to B, 4.5 m (15') to C, 9 m (30') to D, 4.5 m (15') to E (and H), and 4.5 m (15') to F at the END OF TRANSITION. Bracketed values for the 18 m (60') transition are [3 m (10')], [3 m (10')], [6 m (20')], [3 m (10')] and [3 m (10')]. Points B and E are marked with triangles and joined by a dashed straight construction line passing through C and D. The curve A-G-C leaves the baseline at A and passes through G, which is offset from line A-B. A heavy straight stripe runs from C to D. The curve D-H-F passes through H and meets the upper line at F. Points are labeled A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H.

Procedure to install transition: A numbered five-step procedure (see notes).

Title block: City of Pasadena Public Works and Transportation Department, Layout - 3 m [10'] Wide Turn Bay Transition, Standard Plan S-714, Sheet 1 of 1, Revision 1, units DUAL, file S714-1-REV1.DWG 5/24/01, approved by the Transportation Administrator on 6/4/01.
notes:
Procedure to install transition:
1. Lay out points A, B, E, and F.
2. Use points (triangle) B and E to determine a straight line and mark C and D.
3. Mark G and H by measuring in 190 mm (7 1/2 in) [for 27 m (90 ft) and 18 m (60 ft) transitions] perpendicular to lines A-B and E-F.
4. Form curves A-G-C and D-H-F.
5. Stripe.
Note: For 18 m (60 ft) transition, use figures in parentheses shown on diagram and proceed with steps 1 through 5. (The figures for the 18 m (60 ft) transition are drawn in square brackets on the diagram.)
Diagram labels: Start of transition. End of transition. 3 m (10 ft) transition width. Segments 4.5 m (15 ft), 4.5 m (15 ft), 9 m (30 ft), 4.5 m (15 ft), 4.5 m (15 ft) [3 m (10 ft), 3 m (10 ft), 6 m (20 ft), 3 m (10 ft), 3 m (10 ft)].
title: Layout, 3 m [10 ft] Wide Turn Bay Transition
summary: Pasadena layout for striping a 3 m (10 ft) wide turn bay transition. A five-step procedure establishes points A through H, locating the straight line through B and E and forming the curves A-G-C and D-H-F. The diagram is dimensioned for a 27 m (90 ft) transition, using 4.5 m (15 ft) and 9 m (30 ft) segments, with bracketed values for an 18 m (60 ft) transition using 3 m (10 ft) and 6 m (20 ft) segments.

description:
Plan view: A top view of the post, shown as three nested squares for the post (51 mm (2") sq. O.D. (12 gage) sign post), the anchor and the sleeve, with a dashed center line through two holes. The label reads CLEARANCE FROM CURB FACE, with 455 mm (18") DESIRABLE and 305 mm (12") MINIMUM.

Elevation, sign post and sign: A tall square tube post with a sign panel at the top and a second panel just below it. A dimension of 0 mm TO 15 mm (0" TO 1/2") is shown at the top of the post relative to the sign. Two drive rivets (typical) fasten the post at the sign. The vertical clearance from the ground to the bottom of the lowest sign is 2.1 m (7') MIN. (callout 4). A 150 mm (6") dimension is shown at the ground line next to the post base. The label 4 HOLES IN SIGN POST ONLY points at the post below the sign, and TWO (2) DRIVE RIVETS @ 90 degrees points at the connection at ground level.

Installation steps, three elevations at the ground surface: (1) The post anchor, with a hole at the top, is driven 1.0 m (3') into the ground with one hole left above ground for the rivet. It is labeled 57 mm (2 1/4") SQ. O.D. (12 GAGE) ANCHOR SLEEVE. (2) An anchor sleeve 455 mm (18") long is driven over the anchor, labeled 63 mm (2 1/2") SQ. O.D. (12 GAGE) ANCHOR SLEEVE, with TWO (2) HOLES AT 90 degrees IN ANCHOR SLEEVE. (3) The sign post is inserted into the sleeve and fastened with two drive rivets at 90 degrees. Circled step numbers 1, 2 and 3 appear at the base of each elevation.

Title block: City of Pasadena Public Works and Transportation Department, New Sign Post Installation, Standard Plan S-715, Sheet 1 of 1, Revision 1, units DUAL, file S715-1-REV1.DWG 7/8/03, approved by the Transportation Administrator on 7/7/03.
notes:
Notes:
1. Drive sign post anchor into ground approximately 1.0 m (3 ft). Leave one hole exposed above ground for rivet connection.
2. Drive in anchor sleeve which is one size larger than post anchor and 455 mm (18 in) long.
3. Insert sign post and fasten in place.
4. 2.1 m (7 ft) minimum clearance to bottom of the lowest sign.
Labels: Drive rivet (typical). 0 mm to 15 mm (0 in to 1/2 in). Clearance from curb face: 455 mm (18 in) desirable, 305 mm (12 in) minimum. 51 mm (2 in) sq. O.D. (12 gage) sign post. 4 holes in sign post only. Two (2) holes at 90 degrees in anchor sleeve. Two (2) drive rivets at 90 degrees. 57 mm (2 1/4 in) sq. O.D. (12 gage) anchor sleeve. 63 mm (2 1/2 in) sq. O.D. (12 gage) anchor sleeve. 150 mm (6 in) dimension at ground line. Ground surface.
title: New Sign Post Installation
summary: Pasadena detail for installing a new sign post using a driven anchor and anchor sleeve. The anchor is driven about 1.0 m (3 ft) into the ground, an anchor sleeve one size larger and 455 mm (18 in) long is driven over it, and the 51 mm (2 in) square sign post is inserted and fastened with drive rivets. Clearance from the curb face is 455 mm (18 in) desirable and 305 mm (12 in) minimum, with at least 2.1 m (7 ft) from the ground to the bottom of the lowest sign.
